profile.intro: I work on computer vision, visual tracking, and privacy-preserving intelligent systems. I’m a CSE undergraduate and Research Assistant at JKKNIU, building research prototypes and digital platforms that connect technical ideas with everyday needs.
about: My research interests include computer vision, pattern recognition, visual identity tracking, machine learning, and privacy-preserving edge AI. I work under Prof. Dr. Md. Sujan Ali on dataset preparation, experiments, evaluation, and research writing.

Alongside research, I develop web platforms, teach programming, and lead student and community initiatives. I currently serve as President of the 6th Executive Committee of JKKNIU Research Society and founded Amader Online School in 2021.

publications.title: LUMO (Lightweight Unified Multilingual Orchestrator): A Privacy Preserving Offline Voice Assistant
publications.venue: 3rd IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS 2026)
publications.summary: An offline voice assistant combining local speech recognition, a quantized language model, and text-to-speech for English and Bangla interaction on edge hardware.
publications.abstract: Reliable voice interaction is essential in environments with limited internet connectivity and strong privacy. However, most existing voice assistants depend on cloud-based services, which leads to latency issues, dependency on internet access, and privacy vulnerabilities. This research presents LUMO (Lightweight Unified Multilingual Orchestrator), a privacy preserving offline voice assistant designed for edge computing environments. This system integrates local Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR), locally deployed quantized Large Language Model (LLM), and Text-to-Speech (TTS) synthesis into a fully offline pipeline running on a Raspberry Pi 5 with 8 GB RAM. To enable efficient operation on resource constrained hardware, the language model is compressed using 4-bit GGUF quantization, which reduces memory usage while preserving practical conversational capability. Existing edge based voice assistants Mycroft provides partial offline functionality without a generative LLM, with an approximate latency of ~5 s and power consumption of ~12 W, while Rhasspy supports full offline operation but lacks generative capabilities, with ~3 s latency and ~11 W power usage. In contrast, LUMO achieves a Word Error Rate (WER) of 6.8% for short English utterances in low noise conditions, an end-to-end response latency of 2.0-4.0 s, and a lower peak power consumption of approximately 9.0 W. The system also achieves effective offline recognition for Bangla speech, supporting multilingual accessibility in low resource settings. By operating entirely offline, LUMO provides strong data privacy, reduced need for cloud connectivity, and suitability for privacy sensitive edge execution such as rural healthcare, education, and disaster response scenarios.

publications.title: A Machine Learning Framework for Predicting Restaurant Food Waste to Support Sustainable Food Management
publications.venue: 5th IEEE International Conference on Signal Processing, Information, Communication and Systems (SPICSCON 2026)
publications.summary: An exploratory regression framework using operational and contextual data. Evaluation uses a constructed proxy target and does not establish performance against measured restaurant food waste.
publications.abstract: Food waste in the restaurant sector poses a substantial challenge to environmental sustainability and economic efficiency. This paper presents an exploratory machine learning framework for estimating daily restaurant food waste quantities from operational and contextual features. A structured dataset was constructed by integrating restaurant demand records, meteorological data and temporal event indicators, yielding 77,980 records across 27 features. Because large-scale ground-truth food waste measurements are not publicly available, the target variable was derived from operationally justified assumptions, with the complete construction formula and controlled stochastic variability disclosed for full reproducibility. Four supervised regression models, namely Linear Regression, Decision Tree, Random Forest and Gradient Boosting, were evaluated under a chronological 70-30 train-test split that respects the temporal ordering of restaurant operations, augmented by 5-fold time-series cross-validation. All reported metrics are explicitly scoped to performance against the constructed target and do not imply validation against measured food waste. Ensemble methods consistently outperformed linear baselines. Random Forest attained an MAE of 6.19 kg, RMSE of 8.36 kg and R² of 0.817 on the realistic feature subset following systematic exclusion of algebraically leakage-prone variables. Feature importance analysis identified menu diversity, operational area and temporal activity patterns as the primary predictive drivers. The full dataset, target construction formula, codebase and experimental configurations are publicly released to support reproducibility and future extension to empirically measured waste data.

projects.title: SmartPresence
projects.summary: Classroom identity and attendance research using FaceNet-SVM recognition and person tracking.
projects.problem: Maintain identity and estimate attendance across classroom video, including occlusion and face-visibility changes.
projects.approach: Working face-recognition tests and an independent YOLO11n + ByteTrack workflow, with utilities for fingerprint identity lookup and presence-based attendance.
projects.scope: 40-participant experimental setup. Recognition uses 160 × 160 face crops and 128-dimensional embeddings. The configured attendance threshold is 75%.
projects.limitations: Automatic fingerprint-to-track association and the unified end-to-end attendance pipeline remain unconnected in the current repository.

projects.title: LUMO
projects.summary: A privacy-preserving offline multilingual voice assistant for resource-constrained environments.

images.alt: LUMO illustration from the existing portfolio
images.caption: Illustration from the existing portfolio; research code and paper are linked separately.

projects.problem: Support voice interaction where connectivity is limited and speech data should stay local.
projects.approach: Local speech-to-text, local language-model inference, and offline speech synthesis. Research deployment targets Raspberry Pi 5; the repository also includes a Windows implementation.
projects.scope: English and Bangla evaluation data are available in the companion speech-dataset repository.
projects.limitations: Hardware, language, background noise, and utterance length affect results; research and desktop implementations should be distinguished.

projects.title: BITOL · Banana surface-condition detection
projects.summary: YOLOv8n detection and healthy/unhealthy surface-appearance classification for banana images.

images.caption: Examples from the project dataset; boxes are ground-truth annotations, not predictions.

projects.problem: Assess visible banana surface conditions from images.
projects.approach: Object detection with an annotated two-class dataset and repository-hosted experiment evidence.
projects.scope: Repository snapshot: 2,473 images and 5,827 annotated objects. The reported test mAP@50 is 87.04% on the supplied 491-image test split.
projects.limitations: The labels describe appearance and do not establish disease cause, beetle species, or field-wide diagnostic accuracy. The supplied experiment has no separate validation partition.
